name: How to Prepare for Your Interior Refreshing Project

step.name: Step 1: Define Your Vision and Priorities
step.text: Start by thinking about what you want to achieve with this refresh. Is it a cozy reading nook, a more open feel, or simply updated finishes? Consider your lifestyle and how you use each space. Collect inspiration photos, create mood boards, and make a list of what you love and what you want to change. This helps you and your design-build team align on the aesthetic and functional goals from the start.

step.name: Step 2: Measure and Document Your Space
step.text: Accurate measurements are critical to avoid costly mistakes like ordering incorrectly sized furniture or fixtures. Measure room dimensions, ceiling heights, window and door openings, and any existing built-ins. Take photos or videos of the current space. This documentation provides a clear baseline and helps your contractor or designer understand the existing conditions, ensuring new elements fit perfectly.

step.name: Step 3: Establish a Realistic Budget and Timeline
step.text: Determine what you're comfortable investing in your interior refresh, and be honest about it. Research suggests that custom furniture and joinery can have lead times of 8–16 weeks, so factor that into your schedule. Discuss with your contractor early on what’s feasible within your budget and timeline. An experienced team can help you prioritize and explore value engineering options to get the most impact.

step.name: Step 4: Consider Material and Finish Selections
step.text: While aesthetics are important, also think about durability, maintenance, and how materials will integrate with your existing home. Request samples of fabrics, paint colors, flooring, and other finishes to see how they look in your home's lighting. This step helps confirm that your selections are compatible and will stand the test of time, reflecting high-end craftsmanship.

step.name: Step 5: Plan for Contingencies and Communication
step.text: Even the most meticulously planned projects can encounter unforeseen challenges. Build a contingency into your budget and schedule—around 10-15% is often recommended. Equally important is establishing clear communication channels with your chosen design-build team. Understand their process for updates, approvals, and handling any mid-project adjustments.
